description.narrative:
Education Advocacy Network is a Civil Society evidence-based and membership platform created to champion local, national, regional and continental education advocacy agenda. We amplify issue- based campaigns focusing on innovations and strategies for transformative education. Education Advocacy Network is a Strategic partner on the Danida SP II project handling the project education advocacy engagement both at the Sub National and national level. Following the Round table discussion on Education Financing that was held inWest Nile and led by Education Advocacy Network, key issues regarding decision making on policy and resource allocation for the District local governments of Yumbe and Madi Okollo came up. This then required an escalation of these pertinent issues to Ministry of Education and the Ministry of Finance and economic development, hence the National dialogue. This will contribute to the Danida SP project outcome 1.2 "Local and National government are responsive to citizens demands for fiscaljustice to support gender just and pro-poor public spending and service delivery. The theme for the National Dialogue will be: “Exploring opportunities for Sustainable Education financing for refugees and host communities”, the role of Government and Non-government actor. 2.0 Overall objective The overall objective of the high- level national dialogue is to bring together actors at local government and lower local level government levels to engage with leaders at the central government for constructiveengagement on education financing for refugees and host communities.
3.0 Specific objectives for the National high-level dialogue are to; i. Share key issues and recommendations raised by stakeholders at the sub-national round table discussion for action at national level. ii. Strengthen collaboration and meaningful engagement between government and non-governmental actors on education financing for refugees and host communities. iii. Enhance stakeholder participation and engagement on government policy
4.0 Expected outcome of the high -level national dialogue The high- level National dialogue will be delivered to achieve the following outcomes as listed below. i. Discussion and sharing of issues identifiedby the local Participatory Budget Committees established under the DANIDA SP II project with central government officials for action ii. Engagement with government to put in place a multi-sectoral structure to address issues raised by PBCs on addressing educationfinancing at Local government level iii. Securing commitment and practical solutions to education financing for refugee and host community education iv. Development of a position paper to guide further engagement on education financing for refugees and host communities.
5.0 Expected participants The national dialogue will bring together seventy (70) participants drawn from parliament of Uganda, Ministry of Finance, Planning and Economic Development, Ministry of Education and Sports and that of Gender, Labour and Social Development. Other participants will be drawn from the DANIDA SP II project notably, SCBAG, LGF, EAN and community members with specific invitation to learners and teachers who will be selected to attend the national dialogue. Technical and political leaders ofthe two districts, Yumbe and Madi Okollo will also be invited.
6.0 Issues raised at the roundtable discussion at regional level a. Inadequate number of teachers in Madi Okollo District and they recommended that the government puts in place affirmativeaction for recruitment of teachers in Madi Okollo District to improve the quality of Education in the district. b. Inadequate number of desks in schools and they recommended that the government prioritizes purchase of desks to motivate pupils to attendschool as well as avoiding health implications which could result in pupils who seat on dusty floors. c. Poor road network in Madi Okollo District and they recommended that government through UNRA prioritizes the upgrading of the roads as well as increasing funding for the district and sub-county for maintenance of community access roads to enable smooth access to services to the community. d. Poor state of bridges and they recommended that the government constructs the above bridges to ease mobilityfor the road users. e. Dilapidated classrooms and they recommended that the government increases funding for construction of classrooms which can meet the standard set for safety of the learners as well as attract pupils to study in a friendly environmentandstay in school. f. Dilapidated teacher houses and they recommended that the government allocates funding for construction of teacher houses to create a safe environment for the teachers to excellently perform their duties. g. Inadequate clean watersources in the schools and community and they recommended that governmentincreases funding for connection of clean water sources in the schools and communities. h. Limited Secondary schools and only one VTI in Madi Okollo and they recommended that the government speeds up the process of constructing seed schools and also follow the policy of having one secondary school per sub-county so that pupils are motivated to complete their primary education cycle in order to access Secondary schools. Participants also recommended that government constructs more VTIs in Madi Okollo District so that the learners can have access to skills trainings even after P.7. i. Boarder conflict between Uriama Sub-County (Terego District) and Rigbo Sub-County (Madi Okollo District) and they recommended that the government resolves the boarder issues by allocating the three schools and community to a specific district to make implementation in the areas smooth. j. Thematic curriculum is not adequate and is ineffective for refugee children and they recommended that government revises the curriculum to ensure that learners are uniformly taught in English language which will make practicing easier for them.
